headline: US Gov't Lets Private Firms Hack Overseas Cybercriminals
summary: The Trump administration is authorizing private companies to conduct offensive cyber operations against foreign criminal organizations targeting the US.
details: The US government is breaking new ground by allowing private security firms to conduct offensive cyber operations against overseas cybercriminals. This initiative, outlined in a National Security Presidential Memorandum, aims to combat foreign transnational criminal organizations (TCOs) that target US persons, organizations, and government entities.

These private firms will be authorized to perform Cyber Surveillance Operations and Cyber Effects Operations against groups involved in ransomware, sextortion, phishing, financial fraud, and impersonation scams. The memo does not rule out attacks like encryption-based network lockouts or distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks.

To participate, private companies must undergo rigorous vetting by the Departments of Justice and Homeland Security. They must also demonstrate technical proficiency, a proven track record in cyber operations, and maintain facility security and personnel vetting. A key requirement is the deposit of $1 million in an escrow account, which will be forfeited upon non-compliance.

The program explicitly prohibits operations that result in loss of life or serious injury, or that rise to the level of use of force or armed attack under international law. The specifics of the policy are still being defined, with the Justice and Homeland Security departments expected to provide further details within 60 days.

While the move is seen by some as a pragmatic step to combat cybercrime, concerns have been raised about potential conflicts of interest. Some experts note that companies benefiting from the current cybersecurity landscape might lack the incentive to fundamentally change the status quo.

This initiative, outlined in a National Security Presidential Memorandum, aims to combat foreign transnational criminal organizations (TCOs) that target US persons, organizations, and government entities.

The program explicitly prohibits operations that result in loss of life or serious injury, or that rise to the level of use of force or armed attack under international law.
